items.question: A man and a woman are discussing recycling at home.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I spent twenty minutes this morning washing yoghurt pots for the recycling. Is it really worth it?

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I think so. Even if it's a small thing, it makes you more aware of how much you throw away.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I read that most of our plastic never gets recycled at all. The real problem is the companies that produce it.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I agree that companies must do more. They should be forced to use less packaging in the first place.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Right, and with proper fines. Otherwise they'll just carry on.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Still, I don't like it when people use that as an excuse to do nothing themselves.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I'm not saying that. I just think we feel guilty about the wrong things.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Perhaps. But since I started buying loose vegetables at the market, I've saved money too, and that's a perfectly good reason to keep doing it.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Fair point. I used to think it was only about the planet, but saving money is a good motive as well.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Exactly. Whatever gets people started.

statements.text: Sorting rubbish at home makes people notice how much waste they create.

explanation.en: The woman says recycling makes you more aware of what you throw away. The man doubts it is worth the effort.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que reciclar te hace más consciente de lo que tiras. El hombre duda de que merezca la pena.

statements.text: Manufacturers should face tougher rules on packaging.

explanation.en: The woman says companies should be forced to use less packaging, and the man adds "with proper fines".
explanation.es: La mujer dice que se debería obligar a las empresas a usar menos envases y el hombre añade "with proper fines".

statements.text: People often worry about the wrong things when it comes to waste.

explanation.en: The man says "we feel guilty about the wrong things". The woman does not say this.
explanation.es: Solo el hombre dice "we feel guilty about the wrong things". La mujer no lo dice.

statements.text: Saving money is a perfectly good reason to cut down on waste.

explanation.en: The woman calls saving money "a perfectly good reason", and the man says it is "a good motive as well".
explanation.es: La mujer llama a ahorrar "a perfectly good reason" y el hombre dice que es "a good motive as well".

items.question: A man and a woman are discussing ways to keep fit.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I've just joined a gym, but I'm not sure I'll go very often.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Really? I prefer running outside. The fresh air makes me feel much better.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: In winter I'd hate that. It's dark and cold, and I'd never leave the house.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I don't mind the rain, but a gym costs a lot of money.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: It does, but paying every month makes me go. If I didn't pay, I'd stay on the sofa.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Not me. I'd just feel I was wasting money. Although I used to think gyms were boring, and now my brother goes to classes there and loves them.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Classes are the best part! It's more fun with other people.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Maybe I should try one. Anyway, whatever you do, I think sleep matters just as much as exercise.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: I completely agree. I feel terrible when I sleep badly, and then I don't want to exercise at all.

statements.text: Exercising outdoors improves how you feel.

explanation.en: The man says the fresh air makes him feel much better. The woman prefers the gym.
explanation.es: El hombre dice que el aire fresco le hace sentir mucho mejor. A la mujer le gusta más el gimnasio.

statements.text: Dark, cold weather can stop people from doing exercise.

explanation.en: The woman says she would never leave the house in the dark and cold. The man says he doesn't mind the rain.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que no saldría de casa con frío y oscuridad. El hombre dice que no le importa la lluvia.

statements.text: Paying a monthly fee is a good way to stay motivated.

explanation.en: The woman says paying makes her go. The man answers "Not me" and says he'd feel he was wasting money.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que pagar la obliga a ir. El hombre responde "Not me" y dice que sentiría que tira el dinero.

statements.text: Rest is as important for fitness as training.

explanation.en: The man says sleep matters just as much as exercise, and the woman says "I completely agree" and explains why.
explanation.es: El hombre dice que dormir importa tanto como el ejercicio y la mujer responde "I completely agree" y lo explica.

items.question: A man and a woman are discussing holiday lets in their city.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Have you seen what's happened to the old town? Half the flats are now holiday lets.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I have, and I know it's unpopular, but I can't entirely blame the owners. Rents in this city are absurd, and a holiday let pays far more than a long-term tenant.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: That's precisely the trouble. When it's more profitable to host tourists than neighbours, the area hollows out. Shops that served residents close down.

script.speaker: man
script.text: Yes, my local ironmonger has become a souvenir stall. That does bother me.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: So the council should cap the number of nights a flat can be let.

script.speaker: man
script.text: I wouldn't go that far. A cap would be hard to enforce, and it would punish people who rent out a spare room just to get by. I'd rather tax the investors who own dozens of flats.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Hmm. That's more targeted, I'll admit. I'd assumed any tax would simply be passed on to tenants.

script.speaker: man
script.text: It could be, unless it's designed carefully. Tourism isn't the villain, though. The city depends on visitors for thousands of jobs.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: True, but relying on a single industry is risky. One bad summer and the whole economy suffers.

script.speaker: man
script.text: That's fair. If the visitors stopped coming, we'd be in real trouble.

statements.text: Property owners are acting understandably, given how high rents are.

explanation.en: The man says he can't entirely blame the owners because holiday lets pay far more. The woman calls it "the trouble".
explanation.es: El hombre dice que no puede culpar del todo a los propietarios porque el alquiler turístico paga mucho más. La mujer lo llama "the trouble".

statements.text: Local businesses disappear when an area caters mainly to visitors.

explanation.en: The woman says shops for residents close down, and the man gives the example of his ironmonger turning into a souvenir stall.
explanation.es: La mujer dice que cierran las tiendas para residentes y el hombre pone de ejemplo su ferretería convertida en tienda de recuerdos.

statements.text: Limiting the number of nights a flat can be let is a sensible solution.

explanation.en: The woman proposes a cap. The man says "I wouldn't go that far" because it would be hard to enforce.
explanation.es: La mujer propone un límite. El hombre dice "I wouldn't go that far" porque sería difícil de controlar.

statements.text: Taxing large-scale investors would be a better approach than a general limit.

explanation.en: The man says he would rather tax investors who own dozens of flats. The woman only admits it is more targeted and worries about tenants paying.
explanation.es: El hombre prefiere gravar a los inversores con decenas de pisos. La mujer solo admite que es más selectivo y teme que lo paguen los inquilinos.
